title: Set Language, Notation and Venn Diagrams

key_big: ∪ means or, ∩ means and, A′ means not in A.
key_sub: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B): count the overlap once.
body_html:
How it works

  • ξ is the universal set. ∅ is the empty set. n(A) is the number of elements in A.
  • x ∈ A means x is an element of A. B ⊆ A means every element of B is in A (B ⊂ A if B is also smaller than A).
  • A ∪ B (union): in A or B or both. A ∩ B (intersection): in both. A′ (complement): not in A.
  • n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B), so the overlap is not counted twice.
Example

ξ = {1, 2, …, 10}, A = {2, 4, 6, 8} and B = {1, 2, 3, 4}. Find A ∩ B and n(A ∪ B).

A ∩ B = {2, 4}

A ∪ B = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8}

Answer: {2, 4} and 6

Example

In a class of 30, 18 like tea, 15 like coffee and 7 like both. How many like neither?

18 + 15 − 7 = 26 like at least one

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up ∪ (or) and ∩ (and).
  • Counting the overlap twice: n(A ∪ B) is not n(A) + n(B).
  • Taking A′ to mean 'only A'. A′ means everything not in A.
  • Writing 3 ⊂ A instead of 3 ∈ A. Use ⊂ for sets and ∈ for elements.

faq.a: A ∪ B (union) is everything in A or B or both. A ∩ B (intersection) is only what is in both A and B.

faq.q: What is the complement of a set?
faq.a: A′ is everything in the universal set ξ that is not in A.

faq.q: What is the difference between ∈ and ⊂?
faq.a: ∈ links an element to a set (3 ∈ A). ⊂ links a set to a set ({3} ⊂ A).

faq.q: How do I solve Venn diagram word problems?
faq.a: Start with the overlap, then fill in the 'only' regions, then the outside region, and check that all regions add up to the total.

items.q: In a class of 34 students, 16 are in the choir, 8 are in the band and 4 are in both. How many are in neither?
items.e: n(A ∪ B) = 16 + 8 − 4 = 20 (subtract the overlap once). Neither = 34 − 20 = 14.
